verification.summary: The loading-indicator assertion is not falsifiable — it can pass on incidental text containing a period rather than the actual cycling indicator — so the check can report success without the feature; traceability unchecked (no conversation record supplied, only the spec's own quotes).

mustFix.quote: grep -qE '(^|[^.])\.{1,3}([^.]|$)' "$OUT" || { echo "FAIL: no loading indicator observed"; exit 1; }
mustFix.problem: This regex matches any single '.', '..' or '...' substring anywhere in stdout, including inside an ordinary error/status message (e.g. a retry log line ending in 'retrying...'). It does not verify the cycling pattern, its placement distinct from issue lines, or repetition — the assertion the spec's own 'Proves' column claims to check can pass with no indicator implemented at all.

shouldFix.quote: **Whether the loading indicator overwrites the same terminal line or prints new lines** assumed it redraws in place using carriage-return (\r) framing
shouldFix.problem: The spec commits to this framing as the intended behaviour but test.bash never distinguishes \r-framed output from newline-framed output, so an implementation that violates the stated assumption (e.g. prints indicator frames as new lines, polluting the issue-line count) would still pass.

shouldFix.quote: # poll 2 triggers a 500 (backoff should keep it alive); poll after recovery brings the 3rd issue
shouldFix.problem: Comment mislabels which poll triggers the error (the mock fails on the 3rd request, per state["n"] == 3, not the 2nd) — a minor drift between the file and its own commentary, worth correcting so the test file doesn't mislead the next reader.

shouldKnow.quote: plus GITHUB_API_BASE_URL (optional, defaults to https://api.github.com) so tests can point at a local mock server
shouldKnow.problem: This env var and the fixed poll count / mock server topology it enables were invented by the enricher for testability, not requested in any dated entry — flagged already in Assumptions, but worth the operator's explicit sign-off since it becomes a permanent part of the program's env-var surface.
The spec's own meta block already records status: rejected — this review's outcome is consistent with that prior verdict, not a new regression.
